title: Explicit-facet peer geometry and subdivision evidence boundaries
mode: Deeper/broader primary-source research and plan update
scope: Separate classic POLYFACE topology from AcDbSubDMesh control cages and ACIS modeler bodies
Audit authoritative DXF group semantics for POLYFACE, VERTEX, and MESH
Refine optional GDAL DXF projection settings to preserve source identity and avoid block feature truncation
Keep peer execution optional and support evidence route-specific

sources.project: Autodesk DXF reference: POLYLINE, POLYFACE, and VERTEX
sources.observation: POLYFACE is represented through a POLYLINE and child VERTEX records. The references define one-based face indices, negative indices for invisible edges, and zero termination. Writers should place coordinate vertices before face-definition vertices, while readers should tolerate unusual order. A face record is limited to four vertex indices, so larger faces require decomposition.

The AcDbSubDMesh reference documents level-0 cage vertices, faces, edges, crease values, and subentity property overrides. Retention of the base cage and metadata is distinct from evaluating the subdivision surface.

The driver projects POLYFACE to OGR POLYHEDRALSURFACE and 3DFACE to polygon features, exposes EntityHandle and optional raw unhandled values, and documents configurable block inlining/merging. INSERT expansion is capped at 10,000 features per block by default; -1 removes the cap. Binary DXF input is documented beginning with GDAL 3.12. This is a projection route, not a lossless object graph, MESH evaluator, or ACIS kernel.

The project lists MESH among exceptions to its stated R10-R2014 coverage and warns that its writer output for 3DSOLID, REGION, and BODY may not open in AutoCAD. It may be considered only for exact supported parser routes, not a positive modeler writer or MESH evaluator oracle.

existingSubplansRefined: PAR-07/S2/S8: distinguish POLYFACE explicit surfaces, AcDbSubDMesh base-cage retention/evaluated-surface claims, and ACIS carrier/shape claims
PAR-07/S8: optional GDAL projection must pin route/options, remove block feature cap, disable identity-collapsing block expansion, and compare by source handle and block occurrence
Existing POLYFACE and MESH generated test owners remain the local fast-test authorities; no peer-mirroring test is needed
assessment.planImpact: Clarifies that the optional GDAL route can provide a narrowly matched geometry projection for classic POLYFACE only; it does not qualify AcDbSubDMesh evaluation, ACIS semantics, or full document preservation. The existing local tests and implementation sequence remain unchanged.

method.limitations: Research used current public project documentation only. The GDAL binary/runtime was not present or executed, so its projection settings remain an optional recipe. No ACIS body, subdivision surface, or native application semantics were independently exercised.
